newsitem.title: JAPAN: DLR DRIFTS DOWN VS YEN IN TOKYO AS MARK/YEN FALLS.
newsitem.headline: DLR DRIFTS DOWN VS YEN IN TOKYO AS MARK/YEN FALLS.

text.p: 0015 GMT --*Dollar slipped vs yen in early Tokyo on Thursday, hurt by mark's fall vs yen on sales by speculators.
*Stop-loss sales triggered at 62.90 yen pushed down mark to as low as 62.73 yen, its lowest level since July 1995.
*Mark recovered from low on light short-covering, but underlying trend weak.

*"Speculative sales hammered down the mark in thin trade. Downtrend (in the mark) intensified, especially after falling below 62.90 yen, where stop-loss selling orders were triggered," a Japanese city bank dealer said.
*At 0021 GMT, mark stood at 62.93/99 yen compared with 63.06 in New York on Wednesday.
*Dollar fell against yen in tandem to falls in mark/yen, but dollar well-protected around 118.30 yen on short-covering and possible bids by Japanese institutional investors.
*Meanwhile, upside expected to be capped before reaching 119 yen as operators would be reluctant about buying aggressively after overnight falls.
*Dealers said offers lined up around 119.20 yen, with 119.50 yen turning to be strong resistance after failing to break through that level overnight and in Tokyo on Wednesday.
*Dealers said market's focus was shifting back to the trade issue again after U.S.-Japanese trade tensions grew on comments by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky overnight.

*Barshefsky told reporters in Washington that U.S. officials were concerned that car exports to Japan had decreased and the trade deficit with Japan in general was deteriorating. "Obviously we are concerned that Japan not export its way out of its current economic situation."
*Dollar's topside could be limited against yen in short term, with dealers looking towards Japan's current account data for June and first half of 1997 due out on Friday.

*On Wednesday, Lawrence Greenwood, economic minister- counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Tokyo, told Reuters that rises in Japan's current account surplus have the potential to create an explosive situation with the United States.

*"I expect the trade issue will be a key theme the market uses as an excuse to correct the dollar's recent rises. But dollar sentiment is still very strong so there is no reason to sell it aggressively from this point," another dealer at a Japanese city bank said.
*Dollar closed at 118.69/74 yen and 1.8820/30 marks in New York on Wednesday. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
